docs.title: Gateway Overview
docs.text: The Haddacerra Gateway is a hardware platform engineered to interface Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 (CM4) directly with commercial drone controllers such as the DJI RC-N1 and RC-N3

docs.title: 1. Compute & Interposer Stack
docs.text:
• Carrier Board: Houses the CM4, power delivery network, and an integrated 2000mAh battery for independent operation.
  • Networking: Utilizes a dedicated external Wi-Fi module, explicitly bypassing the CM4's default Broadcom chipset to ensure superior network stability and range and usage of 20 MHz band
  • Daughtercard (Interposer): A Pi-Zero sized PCB that acts as the hardware bridge, tapping the DJI controller's telemetry and routing it to the CM4.

docs.title: 2. Enclosure & Display
docs.text:
• Dimensions: 150mm x 85mm x 24mm.
  • Mounting Integration: The enclosure locks directly into the controller's original retractable phone-mounting arm.
  • Enclosure: Houses the physical switches, power button, battery, and a 2.42" OLED status display.
  • Optional SMA Antenna Expansion: The enclosure includes ports to support external panel antennas.

docs.title: 3. Controller & Smartphone
docs.text:
• Host Compatibility: Fully assembled onto a DJI RC-N1, RC-N2, or RC-N3 chassis.
  • Magnetic Device Mount: Because the Gateway enclosure occupies the factory phone clamp, the operator's smartphone or tablet is relocated to a pre-installed magnetic mount on the controller.
  • Wifi Antenna: Uses a compact, high quality stub antenna positioned horizontally on the back of the DJI RC. Keeping it perpendicular to the main vertical drone antennas helps reduce signal interference and maintains a clean wireless connection without disrupting the drone to RC link.

docs.title: Enclosure Specifications & Layout
docs.text: The Haddacerra Gateway enclosure is engineered for mechanical durability, component alignment, thermal dissipation, and for a clean fit on the RC N1-3 series RC's.

docs.title: 1. Physical Dimensions & Form Factor
docs.text:
• Dimensions: 150 mm × 85 mm × 24 mm

  • Form Factor: Compact low-profile box designed for portability and ease of use.

docs.title: 2. Material & Fabrication
docs.text:
• Material: PA12S-HP Nylon.

  • Fabrication Method: HP Multi Jet Fusion (MJF)

  • Post-Processing: Surface-dyed finish for wear resistance and aesthetics.

docs.title: Hardware Safety & Fail-Safe Protection Systems
docs.text:
The Haddacerra Gateway is designed to be straightforward and easy to set up, and to work seamlessly with everything from casual consumer setups like the DJI Mini 2 and Mini 3 up to Mavic 3 Pro and other advanced ground control systems. However, we made sure simplicity never comes at the expense of reliability! safety is our absolute top priority. The system integrates hardware-level protection and fail-safe mechanisms directly onto the daughter card and carrier board to safeguard your equipment and the gateway.

The custom carrier board and daughter card architecture integrate protection logics designed to handle electrical stress and crashes while keeping the operator in full control:

docs.title: 1. ESD & Power Protection
docs.text:
• Channel-Wide TVS Diodes: Every signal, control line and switch is equipped with Transient Voltage Suppression (TVS) diodes, clamping ESD and inductive surges safely to ground.

  • USB Power eFuse & Diode: The USB power input rail incorporates a dedicated active eFuse and reverse-blocking diode to protect downstream components from overcurrent faults and voltage backfeeds.

  • RC Snubber Networks: Used to suppress voltage ringing and transient spikes.

docs.title: 2. Watchdog Heartbeat & Automated NC/NO Latching
docs.text:
To prevent a catastrophic loss during NO mode operation: upon a crash, or software lockup, the system features a hardware-monitored fail-safe loop:

  • Continuous Heartbeat Monitoring: The hardware watchdog continuously checks the operational state of the CM4.

  • Automatic NO-to-NC Emergency Latching: If the hardware watchdog detects a CM4 crash or software lockup while operating in NO mode, dedicated hardware logic forces the circuit back to NC (Passthrough Mode), restoring the manual control signal path independently of CM4 software. The fault state triggers an audible alarm. Follow the documented recovery procedure before resuming operation.

  • Alarm: Once the watchdog trips and latches the gateway to NC mode an alarm will sound a long beep notifying the operator the CM4 has crashed, to stop the alarm return the manual toggle to NC mode, land safely and restart the gateway.

docs.title: 3. DAC Baseline Matching & Glitch Prevention
docs.text:
• EEPROM Calibration: Prior to transitioning control states, the system references stored center-voltage profiles from the onboard DACs EEPROM's.

  • Active Calibration: Dead-zones and center values can shift over time specially on potentiometer type joysticks such as on the RC N1-N3, the gateway will automatically read the RC's new values on every boot and make sure they match if not you will be prompted to match them in the UI and lock the new values in the DAC's EEPROMs.

  • Zero-Step Switching: This allows seamless transition between modes, zero firmware interrupts, the gateway is essentially invisible to the RC even during mode switching and startup.

docs.title: 4. OLED Power & Burn-In Protection
docs.text:
• Voltage-Sensing Gate: The 2.42" OLED display remains completely unpowered unless it detects valid active voltage rails from the RC. Even if the gateway is fully booted, the display stays off if the RC is powered off, eliminating idle wear.

  • 180-Second Idle Sleep: Automatically enters a low-power sleep state if sticks remain untouched for 180 seconds, waking upon any stick movement.

docs.title: Technical Specifications
docs.text: The Haddacerra Gateway is an integrated hardware and telemetry bridging system designed for low-latency control interception, dual-mode switching, and Raspberry Pi integration.

docs.title: Hardware & Compute Architecture
docs.text:
Primary Compute Platform: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 (CM4), mounted on a custom carrier board.

Carrier Board: Integrates the CM4, power-delivery circuitry, internal battery and dedicated Wi-Fi module.

Hardware Interposer: Custom 65 × 30 mm Pi Zero sized daughtercard that connects to the carrier board and handles controller signal interception, switching and monitoring.

Alternative Configuration: A compact assembly using a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W may be considered on request. This is an alternative custom configuration, not the standard Haddacerra Gateway. The CM4-based platform is preferred for the product's reliability requirements.

  • Dedicated Power: Internal rechargeable 2000mAh battrey providing 3-4 hours of operation.

  • Dedicated Wi-Fi Module: Skylabs WG217 Wi-Fi module provides stable and reliable WIFI connection using 20 MHz band on 5GHz.

  • Safety: all lines are ESD protected. Watchdog IC constantly monitors CM4 health. Read more about safety features in safety section.

docs.title: Control Portal UI Reference
docs.text:
The Haddacerra Control Portal (app.haddacerra.com) serves as the client-side interface for managing P2P UDP telemetry, calibration, and monitoring voltage and hardware values.

It is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED TO USE A PC/Laptop as support for external controllers on mobile(Android/iOs) is very tricky and is NOT fully supported.

docs.title: 1. Connection & Latency
docs.text:
The top header provides real-time telemetry health and latancy:

  • UDP Link State: Indicates active or disconnected P2P status.

  • Latency & Jitter: Tracking of packet round-trip latancy.

  • Battery Health: Tracking battery health and remaining charge

docs.title: Stage 1: USB HID Axis Mapping Wizard
docs.text:
• Function: Calibrates and normalizes the connected USB handheld controller inputs across 5 primary channels (AETR + Gimbal Tilt).

  • Operation: Maps stick movements with real-time UI visualizers to verify axis orientation and deadzones.

docs.title: Stage 2: Hardware DAC Voltage Matching
docs.text:
• Function: Calibrates on-board analog outputs to match host transmitter baselines.

  • Operation: Reads center voltages directly from the RC channels, locks in calibration values to onboard DAC EEPROM

docs.title: 3. Telemetry & ADC Monitoring Dashboard
docs.text:
Provides real-time feedback read from the interposer's 12 ADC channels:

  • Passthrough Channels (NC): Monitors voltage levels across manual control lines.

  • Driven Channels (NO): Monitors voltage levels across the DAC output lines.

  • Physical Switch State: Live indication of the state control switch(NC or NO).

  • Power Rail: 12th Channel dedicated to monitor health of the main 5V power rail.

docs.title: 4. Safety & Failsafe Indicators
docs.text:
• Watchdog Status: Confirms active heartbeat pulses from the watchdog IC.

  • Software P2P Health: Monitors P2P UDP tunnel's health

docs.title: Features & Utilities
docs.text: This page describes additional capabilities available through the Haddacerra Gateway Control Panel during active operations.

docs.title: Remote State Override
docs.text:
Remote State Override is an administrative control function accessible through the control panel UI that enables software control over the hardware state mode.

Override Safety Warning

Remote State Override is disabled by default. Activating this feature allows software commands to override physical control toggles. Enable this function only when remote hardware state management is explicitly required.

docs.title: Behavior & Logic
docs.text:
• Initial State: Remote State Override must be manually enabled in the gateway configuration settings before use. When left disabled, all software override commands are ignored.

  • Interposer Logic: Executing the override command bypasses the physical toggle switch position, forcing the gateway into NO mode.

  • Fail-Safe Recovery: If power is lost, or CM4 crashes, the hardware automatically disengages the override and reverts to NC mode.

docs.title: Forget WIFI Network
docs.text: To forget wifi credentials and disconnect from the current active WIFI network, press the dedicated button on the UI, the gateway will be forced into wifi-setup mode where you can re-enter your wifi credentials.

docs.title: Startup Guide
docs.text:
Important: You must power on the Gateway first before turning on the DJI controller. The interposer and CM4 must initialize their bus lines and voltage references prior to the host controller booting up.

Follow these steps to power on, configure network connectivity, and initialize your Haddacerra Gateway system in the field.

docs.title: 1. Power On the Gateway
docs.text: Locate the main toggle switch on the left side of the Gateway enclosure and flip it to the ON position.

docs.title: 2. Connect to WiFi Network
docs.text:
To connect to the CM4 remotely, the gateway requires an active WiFi connection:

  • Automatic Reconnection: Upon boot, the gateway attempts to connect to its last known working WiFi network.

  • Setup Mode Fallback: If the gateway cannot locate or connect to its previous network, it automatically enters setup mode.

docs.title: Network Setup Procedure
docs.text:
1. The gateway broadcasts an open setup network named similar to Haddacera_setupx201.
  2. Connect your phone or computer to this network to automatically open the portal.
  3. Select your local network from the scanned list (or enter the SSID manually), input your WiFi password, and click Submit.
  4. The device saves the credentials and connects to your network, causing the setup network to disappear.
  5. Verify connectivity on the OLED display and the web control panel. If connection fails, the setup network remains active until a successful link is established.

docs.title: 3. Power On the DJI Controller
docs.text: Press and hold the power button on your DJI controller (RC-N1, RC-N2, or RC-N3) as normal. The 2.42" OLED display will illuminate to show the system boot sequence, internal 2000mAh battery voltage, and local network status.

docs.title: 4. Attach Mobile Device
docs.text: Place your smartphone or tablet onto the pre-installed magnetic mount on the controller and connect included USB-C cable.

docs.title: Control Modes (NC & NO)
docs.text:
The Gateway uses hardware switches to control whether stick inputs are routed locally or driven by the onboard CM4 compute core.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Control Layout                    │
├─────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│     NC Mode    │ Controller Sticks ──► Drone (Normal)  │
│                │ CM4 Core          ──► Monitoring Only │
├─────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│     NO Mode    │ Remote / Edge AI  ──► CM4 ──► Drone   │
│                │ Controller Sticks ──► Overridden      │
└─────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 1. NC Mode (Manual Passthrough)
docs.text:
By default, the system operates in NC Mode:

  • The physical controller sticks are wired normally.

  • The operator retains full manual flight authority as normal.

  • The Gateway acts strictly as a telemetry display.

docs.title: 2. NO Mode (CM4 / Remote Control)
docs.text:
To hand off control to an automated script, AI loop, or remote operator:

  1. Instruct the remote user to log in to the control UI at app.haddacerra.com and establish UDP connection.

  2. Locate the state control switch on the left side of the Gateway enclosure

  3. Toggle the state switch to NO Mode.

  4. The interposer will engage the CM4 control lines, allowing the CM4 to send flight commands.

docs.title: Reverting to Manual Control
docs.text:
To instantly restore manual pilot control at any time:

  • Flip the state switch back to NC Mode.

  • RC regains full manual control.

docs.title: Battery and Charging
docs.text:
An internal 2000mah battery is included and will run the gateway for around 3-4 hours of usage on its own.

To charge, connect a USB-C cable from any charger to the port on the right side of the enclosure.

It is possible to use gateway during charging, this way the battery is only being charged and the gateway can run from a wall charger or a larger external battery.

Charging takes about 30-40 minutes.

Make sure to always monitor the battery health on the main status display.

docs.title: Remote Connectivity, Signalling and NAT Traversal
Overview
docs.text:
Haddacerra uses an AWS-hosted infrastructure to establish a UDP communication path between the CM4-based gateway and the remote PC. The connection carries real-time control inputs and telemetry while accommodating the network restrictions commonly encountered on mobile and residential internet connections.

The gateway may operate behind carrier-grade network address translation (CGNAT), where it does not have a publicly reachable IP address of its own. The remote PC may also be behind a NAT or restrictive firewall. A conventional direct UDP connection cannot be assumed to work in these environments.

Haddacerra addresses this problem through connection signalling, NAT traversal and relay infrastructure.

docs.title: Signalling and Connection Establishment
docs.text:
An AWS-hosted signalling service coordinates the initial connection between the gateway and the remote PC. It exchanges the connection information required for the endpoints to discover one another and attempt to establish a working communication path.

Signalling is separate from the control-data stream: it helps establish the session, while the UDP connection carries the operational control inputs and telemetry.

docs.title: ICE and STUN
docs.text:
Where ICE is implemented by the endpoint software, Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) is used to evaluate potential network paths between the gateway and remote PC.

STUN assists an endpoint in discovering the public-facing IP address and port assigned by its NAT device. This information can help the endpoints identify candidate paths for direct UDP communication.

The endpoints exchange connection candidates through the signalling service and perform connectivity checks to determine which candidate pairs can communicate successfully. This allows the software to select a usable path rather than relying on a fixed assumption about network addressing.

docs.title: TURN Relay Fallback
docs.text:
Direct UDP connectivity is not possible in every network environment. Carrier-grade NAT, restrictive firewall rules and particular NAT behaviours can prevent a usable direct path from being established.

When a direct connection cannot be established and the connection procedure supports relay fallback, a TURN server provides an alternative path. The endpoints send their traffic to the relay, which forwards packets between them.

This allows communication to work in many environments where direct endpoint-to-endpoint UDP traffic would otherwise fail. Relay use can add network latency and consumes bandwidth on the relay infrastructure, so the selected route may affect overall control-link performance.

docs.title: Control and Telemetry Path
docs.text:
Once a working path has been established, the UDP communication channel carries real-time control inputs from the remote PC to the gateway and returns telemetry to the remote interface.

The connectivity infrastructure is responsible for establishing and supporting the network path. The gateway's control logic and hardware switching architecture remain responsible for handling the received inputs and managing the local signal path.

Network availability does not override the gateway's control-mode logic or replace its configured timeout and hardware-failsafe behaviour. If connectivity is lost, the gateway's defined timeout and safety mechanisms determine how control returns to the appropriate state.

docs.title: Network Limitations
docs.text:
Connectivity depends on the behaviour of the participating networks, NAT devices and firewalls. The use of signalling, ICE and TURN improves the ability to establish a connection across difficult network topologies, including many mobile networks using CGNAT, but cannot guarantee connectivity through every possible firewall or network policy.

Latency, jitter, packet loss and route selection also depend on the underlying network and whether traffic travels directly between endpoints or through a relay.

docs.title: OLED Display & Power-State Reference
docs.text: The Haddacerra Gateway features an integrated OLED display designed for real-time telemetry readout, system state verification.

docs.title: 1. Power-State Gating & Safety
docs.text:
To prevent screen burn-in and eliminate unnecessary power draw, the OLED display operates under strict conditions:

  • RC-Dependent Activation: The OLED display remains completely powered off unless it detects valid voltage inputs from the RC. If the radio is powered down, the display stays off even when the gateway is active.

  • Instant Wake Trigger: Pressing the RC's power button or turning it on immediately supplies valid voltage levels to the interposer lines, triggering the display to wake up instantly.

docs.title: 2. Idle Timeout & Sleep
docs.text:
The display uses activity monitoring to protect against burn-in during prolonged stationary use:

  • Active Tracking: During standard operation, stick movement keeps the display active.

  • 180-Second Idle Timeout: If the operator leaves the sticks untouched (such as when operating in remote NO mode), the display automatically enters sleep mode after 180 seconds of inactivity. Any subsequent stick movement instantly wakes the panel.

docs.title: 3. Operational Display Modes
docs.text: The OLED interface switches its readout automatically depending on the active control state:

docs.title: NC Mode (Passthrough)
docs.text:
When operating on direct manual control, the screen displays:

  • Battery Health: Real-time power supply status.

  • Link Latency: Round-trip telemetry delay.

  • UDP Connection State: Active/inactive status of the P2P network tunnel.

  • Internet Latency: Network ping performance.

docs.title: NO Mode (Remote / CM4 Control)
docs.text:
When operating via the CM4 or remote internet control, the screen switches to telemetry visualization:

  • DAC Axis Visualizers: Two graphical coordinate boxes with center dots representing live DAC output values (reflecting USB controller stick inputs), allowing direct visual verification of remote or script-driven stick movements.

  • System Status: Battery health and connection integrity readouts.

docs.title: Video Streaming Setup Guide
docs.text:
The Haddacerra Gateway hardware focuses on low-latency stick interception, telemetry routing, and hardware safety overrides only.

Video streaming can be seamlessly integrated using standard RTSP/MediaMTX pipelines.

docs.title: 1. Architecture & Default Server Provisioning
docs.text:
When you initiate a UDP connection through the Web Control Portal (app.haddacerra.com), the system manages RTSP streaming endpoints for low-latency monitoring.

  • Default Managed Server: By default, you can utilize the built-in MediaMTX server provided with the Haddacerra ecosystem. When your UDP connection starts, a QR code containing your unique RTSP link will appear automatically.

  • Self-Hosted Alternative: You are not locked into the default server. If you prefer to run your own server, you can host your own MediaMTX, ignore the provided QR code/link, and point your browser directly to your custom RTSP endpoint.

docs.title: 2. Android Client Setup (Screen Stream App)
docs.text:
To broadcast your mobile device screen and app feed into the streaming pipeline:

  1. Install App: Download and install the Screen Stream application on your Android control device.

  2. Select Mode: Open the app and configure the output to RTSP mode operating as a Client.

  3. Configure URL: Go into the client settings and paste the RTSP server URL obtained from the Control Portal QR code (or your custom server URL).

  4. Initiate Broadcast: Press Start Stream in the app to begin transmitting over the RTSP link.

docs.title: 3. Viewing the Stream
docs.text:
Once the stream is live, you can monitor the video feed using either of the following methods:

  • In-Portal Integration: If using the default server or you entered your custom server URL to the UI, your stream will show on the right side of the UI.

  • Dedicated Browser Tab (Recommended): For a cleaner and larger view open a separate browser tab pointing directly to the stream URL.
